en: Sāmba is our family deity; O Paśupati, we are yours, O Sāmba. I praise Sāmba, by whom the hosts of gods, asuras, and serpents have been delivered. Let there be salutation to Sāmba, offered by me; I worship none higher than Sāmba. I am a follower of Sāmba; my delight is in Sāmba, the Supreme Brahman.
Even the hosts of gods, led by Viṣṇu, were not able to conquer the three cities; O Blessed Śambhu, we are but beasts, and you alone are our Lord.
Then, the gods, having been joined with the Sāla trees, became well-established in mind; therefore, may my heart rest happily in that Supreme Brahman, who is accompanied by Ambā.
The earth is his chariot, the pair of sun and moon its two wheels, Mount Meru his bow, Hari his arrow, and Brahmā his charioteer.
In that [bow], my quiver is the ocean, my horses are the collection of Vedas, and my bowstring is the lord of serpents...
In that [bow], by which the ashes from the body of Aṅgaja (Kārttikeya) were produced as a divine cosmetic; by which the head of the Lotus-born (Brahmā) was accepted along with golden vessels;
and by which the eye of Acyuta (Viṣṇu) was adopted as an offering lotus—in that [bow], may there be prosperity for me.
Having proclaimed, "There is no deity superior to Govinda," Vyāsa raised both his hands and approached the presence of Śiva before the sages;
[I have attained that state] in which Nandīśvara’s hand remained paralyzed and unaltered.
The sky acts like a sword-blade, the expanse of the ten directions acts like fine silk, the moon acts like a flower, and the most steadfast bliss acts as one's own true nature.
In him, for whom the Vedānta serves as a dwelling place and disciplined conduct is his very nature, may my... [devotion be fixed].

(6) Viṣṇu, who by the observance of the Thousand Names of that [Lord], worshipping with lotuses, offered his own eye-lotus among those accumulated [offerings] to His two lotus-feet; and having crushed the host of demons, became the protector of the three worlds—in him may my... [devotion be fixed]. (7)

To that Śauri, whose word is truth, who assumed the form of the boar and out of compassion for all the worlds made himself the Lord visible at his lotus-feet while making the head of Brahmā—whose speech is false, who is unworthy of worship, and who is eternally in the form of a swan—visible; to Him may my... [be offered]. He whose renowned bodies, transformed eightfold, are the earth, water, fire, wind, ether, sun, moon, and so forth, and nothing else exists apart from Him.

Thus concludes the *Daśaślokī-stuti* composed by the venerable Śaṅkarācārya.
